paragraphs: Gridware sells hazard detection to electric utilities, which are expected to maintain near-perfect uptime but typically learn of hazards such as fallen limbs or damaged power lines only after they cause outages or disasters. Its platform gives constant visibility into real-time electrical, physical, and environmental conditions by capturing information directly at the pole.

The company names the problem it targets Hazard Awareness Delay, which it says leads to expensive outages and public safety risks. It calls its own category Active Grid Response, defined by immediate detection, precise localization, detailed identification, and monitoring during outages. The stated payoff for utilities is that crews can get to the right location, with the right gear, armed with the right information.

Gridware says it partners with investor-owned utilities, customer-owned utilities, electric cooperatives, municipal utilities, and public utility districts. It puts its accumulated deployment experience at more than 90 million field hours. Its case studies describe a Puget Sound Energy pilot that the company says improved the utility's ability to identify outages and prioritize repairs during severe weather.

quote.text: Gridware partners with Investor-Owned Utilities (IOU), Customer-Owned Utilities (COU), Electric Cooperatives, Municipal Utilities, and Public Utility Districts to eliminate Hazard Awareness Delay.
